name: ESP32 DevKit V1 (30-pin)
blurb: The common 30-pin ESP32 board with Wi-Fi, classic Bluetooth, a micro-USB port and breadboard-friendly headers.

pins.name: EN
pins.note: Chip enable, the reset line. Pull to GND to restart; not a GPIO.

pins.name: VP
pins.note: Input only, no internal pull-up. Labelled SENSOR_VP on the module. ADC1 channel.

pins.name: VN
pins.note: Input only, no internal pull-up. Labelled SENSOR_VN on the module. ADC1 channel.

pins.name: D34
pins.note: Input only, no internal pull-up. ADC1 channel, fine for sensors with Wi-Fi on.

pins.name: D35
pins.note: Input only, no internal pull-up. ADC1 channel, fine for sensors with Wi-Fi on.

pins.name: D32
pins.note: ADC1 channel, fine for sensors with Wi-Fi on. Touch sensor 9.

pins.name: D33
pins.note: ADC1 channel, fine for sensors with Wi-Fi on. Touch sensor 8.

pins.name: D25
pins.note: DAC output 1. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D26
pins.note: DAC output 2. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D27
pins.note: Touch sensor 7. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D14
pins.note: HSPI clock. Touch sensor 6. Outputs a short pulse at boot. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D12
pins.note: Strapping pin (flash voltage): if something holds it HIGH at power-up the board will not boot. Keep it low or floating at reset. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D13
pins.note: HSPI MOSI. Touch sensor 4. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: VIN
pins.note: 5 V from USB when plugged in (via a diode on most boards). Also where an external 5 V to 12 V supply goes when running without USB; the board regulator drops it to 3.3 V.

pins.name: D23
pins.note: Default SPI MOSI (VSPI).

pins.name: D22
pins.note: Default I2C SCL.

pins.name: TX0
pins.note: UART0 TX, shared with the USB-to-serial chip. It chatters during upload and boot; leave free unless you know you need it.

pins.name: RX0
pins.note: UART0 RX, shared with the USB-to-serial chip. Leave free unless you know you need it.

pins.name: D21
pins.note: Default I2C SDA.

pins.name: D19
pins.note: Default SPI MISO (VSPI).

pins.name: D18
pins.note: Default SPI clock (VSPI).

pins.name: D5
pins.note: Default SPI chip-select. Strapping pin: it outputs a PWM signal at boot and should not be pulled hard at reset.

pins.name: TX2
pins.note: UART2 TX.

pins.name: RX2
pins.note: UART2 RX.

pins.name: D4
pins.note: Touch sensor 0. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D2
pins.note: Drives the onboard blue LED. Strapping pin: an external load that holds it high can block firmware upload. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: D15
pins.note: Strapping pin: pulling it low silences the boot log. HSPI chip-select. ADC2 channel: analogue reads fail while Wi-Fi is on.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.note: Output of the onboard AMS1117 3.3 V regulator. Roughly 400 mA is left after the module's Wi-Fi bursts.

verify: Clone board, no manufacturer drawing or open board file found; layouts vary between factories (USB-C vs micro-USB, 30 vs 38 pins, label spelling). Evidence for the outline is weak: espboards.dev gives 51.45 x 28.33 mm (the figures used here, and likely taken from the same Wokwi data, so not independent), a Mischianti reader comment gives 28.2 x 51.8 mm, and Tinkered gives 51.4 x 28.5 mm; the sources agree on the width within 0.3 mm but not on the length. Not confirmed by any source: row-to-row distance (modelled 25.4), distance from the USB edge to the first pin (modelled 10.09), PCB thickness (modelled 1.6), module and antenna overhang, USB connector size, button positions, the shape heights. With calipers measure: PCB length and width; PCB thickness; centre-to-centre distance of the two header rows; distance from the USB edge to the first pin; how far the module antenna overhangs the PCB; USB connector width. Pin y-positions come from the Wokwi board definition, assumed to start at the antenna end of the PCB. Pin header height is excluded from maxHeight. Supply: 5 V on USB or VIN through an AMS1117-3.3 regulator (espboards.dev); no source gives a current rating, the modelled 110 mA typical and 350 mA peak are estimates (not from a datasheet read here).
sources: https://www.espboards.dev/esp32/esp32doit-devkit-v1/ (opened, reference site: 51.45 x 28.33 mm, 30 pins in two rows of 15, 5 V via USB or VIN, AMS1117-3.3)
https://mischianti.org/doit-esp32-devkit-v1-high-resolution-pinout-and-specs/ (opened: reader comment 28.2 x 51.8 mm, a 30-pin board; schematic reported to be inaccurate)
https://tinkered.ai/components/esp32-devkit-v1 (search snippet only, not opened: 51.4 x 28.5 mm)
